[A] Later authorities cite Zohar: one should not say “I lie on my bed and will study Torah”; one must stand and dress appropriately—“prepare to meet your God, Israel”—and if possible rise on one’s feet, so as not to fall asleep—very good. They also paired morning and evening, day and night, in Torah or prayer. Reshis Chochmah, Shelah, and other musar works elaborate the mitzvah of rising at halachic midnight and punishment for neglect—see there. One who rises at midnight for study should engage in Oral Torah (Shaarei Tzion citing Zohar). Chatzos: Shaarei Tzion cites Zohar—whether summer short nights or winter long—from twelve seasonal hours, Chatzos six hours after actual nightfall; thus night always begins for everyone from true nightfall—“there was evening and there was morning.” Derech Chachmah p. 46 seems to understand summer night beginning some hours before nightfall—hence his question how we pray Minchah in summer within six hours before Chatzos, and why melachah is not forbidden erev Shabbat summer six hours before nightfall—his reasoning is unclear. Zohar and Shaarei Tzion: in winter after twelve hours from nightfall it still belongs to the day for Chatzos and watches. If so we should permit Shacharis before daylight yet in summer delay Shacharis until twelve hours after nightfall—I answer prayer follows instituted times; Shacharis corresponds to seeing daylight as explained later; perhaps hidden reasons exist. In any case Gemara Berachos opening argues with Zohar and holds we reckon night with seasonal hours always—Chatzos is literally half the night—from the Gemara’s question about end of watch… See there. If Zohar—no difficulty—we need a sign for long nights; what does Gemara challenge “Chatzos I arise” vs “my eyes anticipate the watches”? Even rising at Chatzos after six hours from nightfall there are two watches until day on long nights—investigate. Lechem Chamudos, chapter “HaRo’eh”: even if one must rise promptly without laziness, pause briefly and do not stand suddenly after sleep—for Master said end of chapter “One removes five things close to death: ate and rose, drank and rose, slept and rose…” — pause a moment then rise.

[B] “Watchmen for morning” must precede daylight even in summer. If near sunrise say Kinah first then begin “watchmen for morning,” skipping Kinah in between—Rav Hai Gaon; see Responsa Be’er Eshek §124. Kenesses Gedolah siman 219: people who early attend synagogue but doze in prayer—even during Kerias Shema—those are “early risers” in the wrong sense. Properly: if they can intend in prayer they should rise at the watch; but if on Shabbat they come early only to sleep during prayer, better intend when rising in the morning—end quote. See below siman 151 seif 2—sleeping in synagogue forbidden even occasional sleep.

[C] “If he hides … immediately awe reaches him …” I explained at the start of chapter Seder Taanis: the elder says words of “conquest” before them—Rashi: subdues hearts to repentance; Tosafos cite Rav Hai: reveals secrets of their deeds like “hidden lambs of the Merciful”—astounding—is the elder a prophet? Rather I explain: he tells them the Holy One fills the earth with His glory and sees secret deeds—great rebuke that awe should seize him.

[D] “Measure of his sleep …” Shelah p. 124: if he does not wish to sleep he washes hands even while lying down; but it is forbidden to be awake on his bed lying unless thinking Torah. Bach siman 4 cites Tololas Yaakov from Zohar: walking four cubits in the morning without washing is liable for death—why did Beis Yosef not write? Apparently most cannot be careful—better unintentional than intentional—therefore they omitted—his words are strained. Needs study why people are lenient even learned Jews; Levush siman 25 start: immediately upon rising one relieves himself and washes… ordinary people’s facilities are not within four amos of bed—implies leniency. Also Levush siman 8 seif 11: wrapping tallis before washing to avoid four amos without tzitzis—easy to understand. My brother-in-law Rav Yaakov relied on Shach Y.D. §344 citing Mordechai: entire room where body lies counts as four amos—but leniency beyond that room is unclear; Mordechai Berachos 25a Rava: halacha not like Rabbi Shimon—the whole house is four amos—but we hold below siman 79 regarding feces in room… implies specifically room… Likutei Maharil: wherever Gemara says “house” means room. I resolve Mordechai: Berachos opening discusses speaking before the dead only funeral matters—four amos not mentioned—therefore entire room forbidden like within four amos; reason as Beis Yosef—appears hopeless when speaking before dead; where four amos explicit—outside four amos forbidden even in room. Incidentally I summarized in Eliyah Rabbah Y.D. resolving Beis Yosef’s wonder at Mordechai—why tie to first version forbidding entire room—because Mordechai switches Gemara’s wording: first version even mundane speech forbidden before dead—not mockery of poor; appears hopeless—entire room; second version Torah words forbidden because mockery—only within four amos like Kerias Shema near corpse; walking in cemetery with tzitzis/tefillin siman 366 there. This explains Tosafos Berachos 3a s.v. ein… “specifically his four amos”—investigate. I found Damasek Eliezer p. 126a on Tololas Yaakov: perhaps in their time like demons/pairs—so Bach’s wonder why Beis Yosef omitted—people rely; nevertheless God-fearing should be stringent per musar sefarim: prepare two vessels by bed… Etz Chaim: empty vessel should be chipped—it rules the Other Side. Mekor Chayim: do not touch clothes until washing. Seder HaYom: upon rising immediately Modeh Ani… no hand-washing needed even dirty hands—no Name—see end siman 5 what I wrote.
[E] “A little …” Likewise Torah: we ask fixed Torah times—not how many chapters—better five chapters slowly pleasantly than twenty hurriedly (Mekor Chayim).

[F] Parashas Akedah etc.—to remember ancestral merit before God and willingness to surrender soul; Parashas Haman—to believe all sustenance comes from Divine providence. Sefer HaKavanos: say before korbanos; even Shabbat. Shelah p. 202: Shabbat/Yom Tov in sacrifices say only Tamid and what accompanies—musafim and incense—for they are offered Shabbat/Yom Tov; other korban portions do not say even as Torah reading—end quote; Eliyahu Zuta I cited Lechem Chamudos p. 84—one with heart to learn—better learn and suffice with fixed prayers; in place of supplications/korbanos study—Shelah quoted me and asked Gemara separates Torah time from prayer—also contradicts his washing ruling—also found in Tosafos Pesakim: businessman not scholar—need not omit daily maamados/piyutim in siddurim; busy businessman may omit; scholar better study in their place—Tosafos: forbidden say maamodos during Pesukei Dezimra or while chazan repeats—grammarians: if omit daily maamodos say after Tamid daily Psalm—even Shabbat after “On the Shabbat day”; then “You are He who offered incense…” Pitum HaKetores as printed—then no need Musaf even Shabbat—end quote. Taz 132: say before prayer but refined—Tamid parallels blood, prayer parallels limbs—if not both why both—writes incense after Tamid to read between blood and limbs—I wonder—not precise—for when offering Tamid actually they prayed afterward Sukkah 53a; Rabbeinu Yona Berachos explains prayers chiefly parallel blood—still practically correct—not his reason—found Responsa Menachem Azariah §14—see his reason. Seder HaYom: custom say explicitly Levitical song of Temple day—begin weekdays… Responsa Menachem Azariah §25 forbids—see laws of songs. Levush Orach Chayim Va’eschchanan: “tachanun” not Shabbat/Yom Tov means crushing-heart petition; requests for bounty permitted—why Shabbat maamodos arranged petitions.

[G] Ten Commandments etc.—Eliyahu Zuta I wrote Maharshal said them before Baruch Sheamar because ten “Baruch” until “Blessed are You God”—his ancestor erred about my words—see there. Arizal students: daily four remembrances—Matan Torah, Amalek, Miriam’s leprosy “remember what God did to Miriam,” Yetzias Mitzrayim—end quote. Shelah p. 228: printed siddur after 72 verses sealed “Blessed are You who hears prayer”—other petitions similarly sealed—mistake—no Gemara source—bracha levatala—say “Blessed are You who hears prayer” without Name—end quote; see below siman 46 seif 7 and Taz end 131.
[H] “But forbidden …” lest they say “Torah is only this”—therefore not written on synagogue pamphlet (Lechem Chamudos).

[I] “The sacrifices …” Scripture writes “This is the law of the Chatas”—why “law”? Not “chukah”—reading is like offering; Rashi: “Torah” not “chukah”—therefore inferred—but Levush: Torah did not make them mere unexplained statute but law with revealed reason. Eliyahu Zuta: I settled Rashi—like Mizrachi Chukas—anything written “Torah” without “chukah” alone has reason; Gemara Menachos 19 challenges “everywhere chukah and Torah nothing adds”—korbanos written “Torah” yet do not add—inference Torah needs chukah… Eliyahu Zuta elaborated—see there; my honored father explained Rashi learns from word “Torah”—difficulty for Rashi: perhaps “Torah” teaches obligation from study—answers because not written “chukah”—meaning from Torah alone we do not learn obligation except from “chukah”—sharp explanation.
